title: Student Privacy & Campus Surveillance Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Protect your student data and privacy from campus surveillance. Complete checklist for educational privacy, digital proctoring, and data rights.
intro: Educational institutions collect vast amounts of student data and deploy extensive surveillance systems. This checklist helps you understand your privacy rights, protect your personal information, and navigate campus monitoring while maintaining your digital privacy.

items.task: Understand your FERPA rights and how to access your educational records
items.why: FERPA gives you control over your educational records and limits how schools can share your information with third parties.
items.howTo: Request a copy of your school's FERPA policy. Learn what information is considered 'directory information' and how to opt out of public disclosure. Submit written requests to access your records.

items.task: Audit what personal data your school collects and stores
items.why: Schools collect extensive data beyond grades, including biometric data, location tracking, and behavioral analytics that could impact your future.
items.howTo: Review your student handbook and privacy policies. Request a data audit from the registrar's office. Check what information is shared with third-party vendors and partners.

items.task: Opt out of directory information disclosure
items.why: Directory information can be shared publicly without your consent unless you explicitly opt out, potentially exposing personal details.
items.howTo: Submit a written request to your registrar's office to suppress directory information. This typically includes your name, address, phone, email, and enrollment status from public disclosure.

items.task: Limit third-party data sharing and vendor access
items.why: Educational technology companies often collect student data for analytics, advertising, or other commercial purposes beyond education.
items.howTo: Review contracts with EdTech vendors. Request information about data sharing agreements. Opt out of non-essential services that collect personal data when possible.

items.task: Map campus surveillance systems and monitoring zones
items.why: Understanding surveillance infrastructure helps you make informed decisions about privacy in different campus areas.
items.howTo: Identify security cameras, WiFi monitoring zones, card reader locations, and facial recognition systems. Request surveillance policies from campus security and IT departments.

items.task: Minimize student ID card tracking and data collection
items.why: Student ID cards often contain RFID chips that track your location and activities across campus, creating detailed behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: Store your ID card in an RFID-blocking wallet when not in use. Only swipe for essential services. Request information about what data is collected and how long it's retained.

items.task: Secure your connections on campus WiFi networks
items.why: Campus networks often monitor internet activity and may log your browsing history, creating privacy risks.
items.howTo: Use Incognito Browser for sensitive browsing. Connect through a VPN when possible. Avoid automatic WiFi connection to prevent constant location tracking. Use cellular data for private communications.

items.task: Opt out of biometric data collection systems
items.why: Fingerprint scanners and facial recognition systems create permanent biometric profiles that could be breached or misused.
items.howTo: Research alternative authentication methods like PIN codes or traditional ID cards. Submit formal opt-out requests for biometric systems. Understand your state's biometric privacy laws.

items.task: Understand and limit digital proctoring surveillance
items.why: Proctoring software monitors your screen, camera, microphone, and system activity, often storing recordings and creating privacy risks.
items.howTo: Review proctoring software privacy policies. Request information about data retention and sharing. Use a dedicated computer or browser profile. Cover cameras when not testing.

items.task: Configure privacy settings in learning management systems
items.why: LMS platforms track detailed learning analytics including time spent, click patterns, and engagement metrics that create behavioral profiles.
items.howTo: Review privacy settings in Canvas, Blackboard, or other LMS platforms. Limit profile visibility to instructors only. Disable optional tracking features and social components.

items.task: Isolate school-issued devices from personal data
items.why: School devices often have monitoring software that can access personal files, browsing history, and communications.
items.howTo: Use school devices only for academic purposes. Never save personal files or log into personal accounts. Use Incognito Browser or private browsing mode. Consider separate user accounts.

items.task: Secure your academic communications and collaboration
items.why: School email and collaboration platforms are monitored and archived, potentially exposing private conversations and personal information.
items.howTo: Use school email only for academic purposes. Avoid sensitive topics in school communications. Use personal encrypted messaging for private discussions with classmates.

items.task: Plan data deletion and account closure after graduation
items.why: Schools may retain your data indefinitely unless you take action to request deletion of non-essential information.
items.howTo: Create a checklist of all school accounts and services. Request deletion of non-academic data after graduation. Download important files before account closure. Update contact information selectively.

items.task: Advocate for stronger student privacy policies
items.why: Collective action can improve privacy protections for all students and create institutional change in data practices.
items.howTo: Join or create student privacy advocacy groups. Attend school board meetings. Propose privacy policy improvements through student government. Share privacy concerns with administrators.
